highlights: DeepSeek released DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017, a minor update to DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with gains across reasoning, coding, agentic tasks, and visual benchmarks. The Youtu-Parsing-Omni paper reports state-of-the-art results on OmniDocBench v1.6 with a single 5 B-parameter checkpoint, and the LOWN paper reports retaining 99.6% of LLaDA-V's score at 35.3% of the decoding FLOPs.

LangChain shipped langgraph==1.2.19 and langgraph-sdk==0.4.11, both focused on stream and reconnection handling fixes, and the Soft-MTP paper proposes a one-line MTP change that removes the noisy residual gradient without adding parameters.

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 is a minor update to DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash , delivering substantial improvements across reasoning, coding, agentic tasks, and visual benchmarks.

Alongside these gains, the model reduces task execution time and output length, enabling users to complete tasks faster and at lower cost and advancing the performance–cost Pareto frontier across multiple agent harnesses.
This release does not include a Jinja-format chat template.
For production use, we additionally release deepseek-recipe , a set of Rust libraries with Python bindings that provides the same prompt format as a maintained, protocol-aware toolkit.

items.title: Youtu-Parsing-Omni parses documents, images, audio, and video with one encoder
items.summary: Youtu-Parsing-Omni converts documents, images, audio, and video into structured records grounded in space and time, using one encoder for every modality and one schema for every task. With a single 5 B-parameter checkpoint it reaches state-of-the-art performance on OmniDocBench v1.6 (96.96 Overall) and leads open-weight models on OmniParsingBench (75.08 Avg.), and code and model weights are publicly available.

evidence.quote: Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small We present Youtu-Parsing-Omni, an omni-modal parser that converts documents, images, audio, and video into structured records grounded in space and time, providing a perception layer for agents that read, locate, and cite evidence across modalities.

Youtu-Omni-Encoder, initialized from a pre-trained language model to strengthen text reading, encodes all modalities with shared weights in a unified space-time coordinate system, and a few fusion layers let video frames attend to concurrent audio, bringing cross-modal fusion and temporal alignment

OmniSchema unifies the outputs of all ten parsing tasks, allowing a single self-evolving post-training procedure, OmniSchema-Aware On-Policy Distillation (OSAD), to provide a shared token-role-based objective across tasks.

With a single 5 B-parameter checkpoint, Youtu-Parsing-Omni achieves state-of-the-art performance on OmniDocBench v1.6 (96.96 Overall) and leads all open-weight models on OmniParsingBench (75.08 Avg.), with its advantage concentrated on audio and video.
Code and model weights are publicly available.

Strong results at a small size – state-of-the-art on OmniDocBench v1.6 (96.96 Overall), best open-weight model on OmniParsingBench (75.08 Avg., second only to Gemini-3-Pro), and competitive with specialized models on chemical-structure (ChemOCR) and music-score (PDMX-Synth) recognition ( results ).
Easy to serve – a vLLM plugin, pinned serving settings, task prompts and inference examples are included.

items.title: Liquid AI releases LFM3-Omni-2B for on-device multimodal use
items.summary: LFM3-Omni-2B is Liquid AI's first omni-modal model in the LFM3 family: a single end-to-end model that understands text, images, video and audio, and answers in text and speech. At 2.2B parameters it is designed to run efficiently on phones, laptops and other edge hardware, replacing separate ASR, vision-language, LLM and TTS models with one.

items.title: Claude Code v2.1.316 adds subagent effort controls and pooled gateway budgets
items.summary: The v2.1.316 release adds CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_EFFORT to set the effort level subagents run at, pooled group budgets for the Claude apps gateway, and a layered managed.policy_mode. It also fixes shell commands left running on macOS and Linux when Claude Code exits by itself, and fixes models on Vertex AI and Amazon Bedrock showing an error instead of switching to an older model.

evidence.quote: Added CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ULTRATHINK , which turns the ultrathink keyword off
Added pooled group budgets to the Claude apps gateway: one monthly budget that a group's members share, on top of each member's own limit, set with pooled_budget on the spend limits admin API
Added CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_EFFORT to set the effort level subagents run at when nothing else names one, instead of inheriting the session's
Added managed.policy_mode: layered to the Claude apps gateway: every policy that matches a developer applies, each merged over the ones listed below it, not only the first
Fixed shell commands being left running on macOS and Linux when Claude Code exits by itself, for example when credentials are refused or a cloud session is archived
Fixed bash aliases with line breaks in their value (except in Git Bash), and functions whose names start with a dash, being garbled or lost in the Bash tool's shell
Fixed sonnet , opus and haiku on Vertex AI and Amazon Bedrock showing an error mid-session instead of switching to an older model when the newest is not yet available to the account or region

items.title: LOWN routes image processing only when diffusion VLMs need it
items.summary: LOWN decides at every decoding step whether to process the image and how many tokens to unmask, predicting masked tokens without the image and processing it only when that prediction disagrees with the last image-conditioned prediction. Without training or a tuned threshold, it retains 99.6% of LLaDA-V's score on ten benchmarks at 35.3% of the decoding FLOPs and cuts generation time by 57.4% on average.

evidence.quote: To measure how often the image is actually needed, we compare LLaDA-V 's predictions with and without the image at every decoding step and find that removing the image changes a token being unmasked at only 22.8% of steps on average and at as few as 7.9%.
We therefore propose LOWN , a decoding method that decides at every step whether to process the image and how many tokens to unmask.
LOWN predicts the masked tokens without the image and processes the image only when this prediction disagrees with the last image-conditioned prediction.
Without training or a tuned threshold, LOWN retains 99.6% of LLaDA-V 's score on ten benchmarks at 35.3% of the decoding FLOPs on average.

items.title: IDM adds moment matching to distribution matching distillation
items.summary: Intrinsic Distribution Matching (IDM) retains the full DMD correction and matches feature means and per-coordinate standard deviations using the generator's exponential-moving-average (EMA) copy, requiring no external feature encoder. At two network evaluations it reaches 94.25% and 90.20% on Chinese and English LongText-Bench with full-parameter and LoRA tuning on Z-Image-Turbo 6B and Qwen-Image 20B.

evidence.quote: We introduce Intrinsic Distribution Matching (IDM), which retains the full DMD correction and matches feature means and per-coordinate standard deviations using the generator's exponential-moving-average (EMA) copy, requiring no external feature encoder.
Experiments use full-parameter and low-rank adaptation ( LoRA ) tuning on Z-Image-Turbo 6B and Qwen-Image 20B.
At two network evaluations, IDM reaches 94.25% and 90.20% on Chinese and English LongText-Bench , the highest scores among the compared methods at this budget.
Controlled ablations show gains from the added moment loss, while generator EMA features perform competitively with an external DINOv2 encoder across the five reported metrics.

items.title: Soft-MTP removes the noisy residual in multi-token prediction training
items.summary: Soft-MTP is a one-line code change to MTP that removes the noisy residual from the MTP gradient and backpropagates only the KL self-distillation signal by reusing existing NTP and MTP cross-entropy computations. It supports both DeepSeek- and Meta-style MTP, adds no parameters, and incurs no measurable overhead.

evidence.quote: We identify a flaw in standard MTP training, in which a residual component of the MTP gradient interferes with both next-token and multi-token learning, increasingly so with scale.

Specifically, the MTP cross-entropy gradient can be decomposed exactly into a KL self-distillation term that pulls each MTP head toward the model's own next-token prediction (NTP) distribution and improves speculative decoding , and a residual that has a low signal-to-noise ratio and buries the usef

We introduce the KL gradient-recovery trick: when two distributions share a linear output head, the gradient of their KL divergence can be recovered exactly by combining their cross-entropy gradient s through straight-through gradient routing .

This enables Soft Multi-Token Prediction ( Soft-MTP ), a one-line code change to MTP that removes the noisy residual and backpropagates only the KL self-distillation signal by reusing the existing NTP and MTP cross-entropy computations.
Soft-MTP supports both DeepSeek- and Meta-style MTP, adds no parameters, and incurs no measurable overhead.

items.title: A Nemotron-based voice character runs on a single workstation
items.summary: The character is built on the NVIDIA Nemotron Voice Agent with NVIDIA Nemotron ASR, Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B 4GB, Magpie TTS Zeroshot and Audio2Face-3D, and runs on a single workstation. Its median end-of-speech-to-audio latency is 1.70 seconds with Bolt Q4 & TTS, and 0.72 seconds for cached responses.

evidence.quote: He is built on the NVIDIA Nemotron Voice Agent with NVIDIA Nemotron ASR , Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B 4GB , Magpie TTS Zeroshot and Audio2Face-3D , and he runs on a single workstation.
Listening: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 ASR turns visitor speech into text.
Thinking: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B 4GB , an open small language model for conversational agents, writes each reply.
Speaking: NVIDIA Magpie TTS Zeroshot voices each reply from a short reference sample of the character.
Animating: NVIDIA Audio2Face-3D turns clean speech into mouth animation in Unreal Engine 5.
It is an open small language model purpose-built for local conversational agents and interactive characters, which is a fair description of a talking garage door.
I use the 4-bit quantized release (the “4GB” in its name) as the default response model, with the BF16 checkpoint available for comparison.

items.title: LangGraph releases langgraph==1.2.19 and langgraph-sdk==0.4.11
items.summary: The langgraph==1.2.19 and langgraph-sdk==0.4.11 releases focus on streaming and reconnection fixes. The SDK now retries runs.wait, join and cancel(wait=True) reconnects with backoff, preserves SSE data and cursor state across chunks, and retries failed stream reconnects with backoff.
